WILLIAMSILENT.name: William of Orange
WILLIAMSILENT.summary: Prince of Orange and principal leader of the Dutch Revolt against Philip II. His political leadership helped lay the foundations of the future Dutch Republic.
sections: In the service of Charles V

Born at Dillenburg in 1533, the son of the Count of Nassau, he inherited the Principality of Orange and extensive estates in the Low Countries in 1544. Educated at the court in Brussels, he became a trusted servant of Charles V and served under Philip II as stadtholder of Holland, Zeeland and Utrecht.

He opposed the crown’s religious policy and the government of Granvelle. When the Duke of Alba arrived in 1567, William withdrew to Germany and from 1568 led armed resistance. The towns of Holland and Zeeland recognised him as stadtholder in 1572, and in 1573 he publicly embraced Calvinism.

He promoted the Pacification of Ghent in 1576 and, after the Union of Utrecht in 1579, the formal break with Philip II through the Act of Abjuration in 1581. Philip had outlawed him in 1580. Balthasar Gérard assassinated him at Delft in 1584; his son Maurice continued the war.

governmentNotes.Cargo provincial delegado por los Estado: Provincial post delegated by the States, with documented personal areas and dates; not hereditary sovereignty over the entire Republic or the Spanish provinces.

MARIAARAGINF.name: Maria of Aragon
MARIAARAGINF.summary: Daughter of the Catholic Monarchs, born in Córdoba in 1482, she married Manuel I of Portugal in 1500 after the death of her sister Isabella. She was the mother of John III of Portugal and Empress Isabella, and died in Lisbon in 1517.

JOHN1FOIX.name: John I of Foix
JOHN1FOIX.summary: The son of Isabella de Foix-Castellbó and Archambaud of Grailly, he continued the heritage of Foix under a new male descent. His marriage to Juana de Albret connected both houses before the navarra royal union of the end of the 15th century. His son Gastón IV married Leonor of Navarre.

governmentNotes.Carlos VII de Francia le concedió el con: Charles VII of France granted him the county in 1425.

MARIAAUSTESP.name: Maria of Austria
MARIAAUSTESP.summary: A consort of House Habsburg whose life was connected with Holy Empire, Austria.

CARLOSVAL.name: Charles of Valois
CARLOSVAL.summary: Although he never reigned, he accumulated dynastic projects and considerable influence in the French court. His son Philip VI inaugurated the Valois dynasty.

GODOFREDO2BRET.name: Geoffrey II of Brittany
GODOFREDO2BRET.summary: Fourth son of Henry II and Leonor of Aquitaine, he ruled Brittany since his marriage to Duchess Constance in 1181. He participated in the rebellions against his father and died in Paris in 1186; his posthumous son Arthur inherited his rights.

governmentNotes.Por su matrimonio con la duquesa Constan: For her marriage to Duchess Constance in 1181.

ALAINALBRET.name: Alain I of Albret
ALAINALBRET.summary: Known as Alain the Great, he inherited the lordship of Albret through the line of John of Tartas and Charles II. He married Françoise de Châtillon and sought to expand his house’s political position.
ALAINALBRET.biography: Known as Alain the Great, he inherited the lordship of Albret through the line of John of Tartas and Charles II. He married Françoise de Châtillon and sought to expand the political position of his home. His son John III came to Navarre royalty by his marriage to Catherine; his daughter Carlota married Caesar Borja.

GASTONVIANA.name: Gaston of Foix, Prince of Viana
GASTONVIANA.summary: The son of Gaston IV of Foix and Eleanor of Navarre, he married Magdalene of France and was the father of Francis Phoebus and Catherine. He died before his mother succeeded to the Navarrese throne, so his rights passed to his children.

MARIADEMEDICI.name: Marie de’ Medici
MARIADEMEDICI.summary: Daughter of the Grand Duke Francis I of Tuscany and second wife of Henry IV of France. Regent for his son Louis XIII after the assassination of the king in 1610, she was banished after facing Richelieu.

PETRUTANAR.name: Petru the Younger
PETRUTANAR.summary: The son of Mircea Ciobanul and Chiajna, he accepted the principality at the age of twelve. His mother maintained a decisive intervention in the government.
PETRUTANAR.biography: The son of Mircea Ciobanul and Chiajna, he agreed to the principality at the age of twelve. His mother maintained a decisive intervention in the government. Ottoman authority deposed him in 1568 and died that same year in exile. His trajectory allows us to distinguish the young holder from the one who led much of the politics.

SIBYLLAARM.name: Sibylla of Armenia
SIBYLLAARM.summary: Daughter of Hetum I and wife of Bohemundo VI. Her marriage reinforced the alliance between Armenia, Antioch and Tripoli; after the death of her husband she intervened in county politics during the Bohemundo VII minority.

GUILLERMO5BAV.name: William V of Bavaria
GUILLERMO5BAV.summary: William the Pious, Duke of Bavaria between 1579 and 1597. He promoted the Counter-Reform and the Jesuit Church of St. Michael in Munich; he abdicated in favour of his son Maximilian.

MARIAAUSTRIACLEVES.name: Maria of Austria
MARIAAUSTRIACLEVES.summary: A consort of House Habsburg whose life was connected with Austria, Jülich, Cléneris.

ANAAUSTRIABAV.name: Anna of Austria
ANAAUSTRIABAV.summary: A consort of House Habsburg whose life was connected with Bavaria, Austria.

JUAN6BRET.name: John VI of Brittany
JUAN6BRET.summary: Son of John IV and Joan of Navarre, he ruled Brittany during a decisive phase of the Hundred Years' War. His marriage to Joan of France reinforced the connection with the Valois. He appears as John V or John VI according to the ducal numbering adopted; the two names correspond to the same person.

TOMASFRANCISCOSAB.name: Thomas Francis of Savoy-Carignano
TOMASFRANCISCOSAB.summary: A younger son of Charles Emmanuel I and Catherine Michelle of Spain, he founded the Savoy-Carignano branch. He married Marie de Bourbon, Countess of Soissons, and took part in the disputes over the regency of Christine of France.
TOMASFRANCISCOSAB.biography: The youngest son of Charles Emmanuel I and Catherine Michelle, began the Savoy-Carignano branch. He married Marie de Bourbon-Soissons and participated in the disputes against the regency of Christine of France. His military career alternated alliances in a context of European war; his offspring would arrive much later on to the Sardinian throne with Carlos Alberto.

BLANCACAST.name: Blanche of Castile
BLANCACAST.summary: Queen consort and regent of France, and a daughter of Alfonso VIII of Castile. She governed during Louis IX’s minority and absences and firmly defended the authority of the Capetian monarchy.

GULKHANEUDOKIA.name: Gulkhan Eudoxia of Georgia
GULKHANEUDOKIA.summary: Georgian princess, took the name Eudoxia and married Manuel III. She was the mother of Alejo IV. Her file connects two Black Sea courts without attributing a territorial government to her for her status as consort.

AMEDEO4SAB.name: Amadeus IV of Savoy
AMEDEO4SAB.summary: He succeeded Thomas I and had to negotiate with his brothers the distribution of family rights. His Italian policy brought him closer to Frederick II.
AMEDEO4SAB.biography: He succeeded Thomas I and had to negotiate with his brothers the distribution of family rights. His Italian policy brought him closer to Frederick II. He left the county to his son Boniface, still minor; his daughter Beatriz first linked with Saluzzo and then with Manfredo of Sicily, creating two different Mediterranean connections.

JEANNEALBRETFOIX.name: Joan of Albret, Countess of Foix
JEANNEALBRETFOIX.summary: The daughter of Charles I of Albret, she married John I of Foix and was the mother of Gaston IV. This marriage connected the Albret with the Foix-Grailly line before the later link of Catherine of Navarre and John III of Albret. Her presence reveals a family connection prior to the most well-known royal union.

FRANCESCOSAL.name: Francis of Saluzzo
FRANCESCOSAL.summary: Brother of Michael Anthony and John Louis, he acceded to the Marquisate of Saluzzo with French support after the succession crisis of 1528. His later rapprochement with the emperor changed that alignment.
FRANCESCOSAL.biography: Brother of Miguel Antonio and Juan Ludovico, he acceded to the marquis with French support after the succession crisis of 1528. His subsequent approach to the emperor changed that relationship. The succession passed to Gabriel, favored by France, while Juan Ludovico continued to defend his own rights. The conflict of the brothers weakened the autonomy of the marquisate.

BONASABOYA.name: Bona of Savoy
BONASABOYA.summary: A consort of House Savoy whose life was connected with Milan.

MARGFOIXBRET.name: Margaret of Foix, Duchess of Brittany
MARGFOIXBRET.summary: A daughter of Gaston IV of Foix and Eleanor of Navarre, she married Francis II of Brittany and was the mother of Anne of Brittany. Her position provides a direct link between the Pyrenean houses and the Breton succession.

ALICECHAMPJER.name: Alice of Champagne
ALICECHAMPJER.summary: Daughter of Henry II of Champagne and Elizabeth of Jerusalem, he married Hugo I of Cyprus. He exercised regency functions and maintained rights and interests linked to both shores of the Mediterranean. His file connects the house of Champagne with Cyprus and Jerusalem, without reducing it to its later Navarre branch.

GUILLERMO3HENAO.name: William I of Hainaut
GUILLERMO3HENAO.summary: Count of Holland, 1304–1337. Count of the Avesnes dynasty.

GASTON2FOIX.name: Gaston II of Foix
GASTON2FOIX.summary: He inherited Foix and Bearne as a child and was the father of Gastón Fébus. His marriage to Leonor de Comminges connected the Foix to another house in the Pyrenean realm. His death in 1343 opened the minority of his son, during which Leonor had a role of government.

MARGDUR.name: Margaret of Durazzo
MARGDUR.summary: A widow of Charles III, he exercised the regency of Naples by his son Ladislao. The dispute with the branch of Anjou forced to sustain power from reduced bases and to negotiate supports; his intervention preserved the rights of the house of Durazzo.

CONSTPRINCEIMER.name: Constantine, Prince of Imereti
CONSTPRINCEIMER.summary: The son of Bagrat III, belonged to the generation that disputed Western power to his relatives. His sons Rostom and George III successively occupied the throne, maintaining the genealogical continuity of the royal house.

GERALD9KILDARE.name: Gerald FitzGerald, IX Earl of Kildare
GERALD9KILDARE.summary: He inherited the influence of his father and repeatedly exercised the delegated government of Ireland. Henry VIII’s distrust of his power ended in his arrest. His son Thomas’ rebellion precipitated the collapse of the family position.

ADOLFHOLGOTT.name: Adolf of Holstein-Gottorp
ADOLFHOLGOTT.summary: Duke of Holstein, 1544–1586 (rama), Duke of the Holstein-Gottorp dynasty.

CARLOSM.name: Charles Martel of Anjou
CARLOSM.summary: A noble of House Anjou-Hungary whose life was connected with Naples.

FEL3FRA.name: Philip III of France
FEL3FRA.summary: He inherited the French crown during the crusade in which Louis IX died. His intervention against the Crown of Aragon ended in a disastrous campaign and in his own death.

JUANAAUST.name: Joanna of Austria
JUANAAUST.summary: An infanta of House Habsburg whose life was connected with Spain, Portugal.

EUGENIOMAURICIOSAB.name: Eugene Maurice of Savoy-Carignano
EUGENIOMAURICIOSAB.summary: Son of Thomas Francis of Savoy-Carignano, he inherited from his mother the county of Soissons and served as a general in the armies of Louis XIV. He married Olympia Mancini, niece of Mazarino, and was the father of Prince Eugene.

governmentNotes.Heredó el condado por su madre, María de: He inherited the county by his mother, Marie de Bourbon-Soissons.

MARGTERESAAUT.name: Margaret Theresa of Austria
MARGTERESAAUT.summary: A consort of House Habsburg whose life was connected with Spain, Holy Empire, Bohemia.

WILLIAM1NETHERLANDS.name: William I of the Netherlands
WILLIAM1NETHERLANDS.summary: Son of Stadtholder William V, he was proclaimed the first King of the Netherlands in 1815, when the kingdom also included Belgium, and became Grand Duke of Luxembourg. The Belgian Revolution of 1830 separated the south; he abdicated in 1840.

LUIS8FRA.name: Louis VIII of France
LUIS8FRA.summary: Before reigning in France, he accepted an invitation from English barons to dispute the throne to John without Land. Already as king, he continued the expansion of the capedom in southern France.

GERALD15DESMOND.name: Gerald FitzGerald, Earl of Desmond
GERALD15DESMOND.summary: Their confrontation with the expansion of Tudor power led to Desmond’s rebellions. Defeat, his death and subsequent confiscations transformed Munster. FitzGerald earldom is distinguished from the former MacCarthy kingdom.

ANAFOIX.name: Anne of Foix-Candale
ANAFOIX.summary: Belonging to the branch of Foix-Candale, he married Ladislaus of Hungary and Bohemia. He was the mother of Louis II and Anna, future wife of Ferdinand of Habsburg. His marriage brought the connections of a French southwest house to the center of Europe and to the generation of the crisis of 1526.

MARGFRAFLA.name: Margaret of France
MARGFRAFLA.summary: Countess of Artois, 1361–1382. Countess of the Capeto Dynasty.

ISABELMONSAL.name: Isabella of Montferrat
ISABELMONSAL.summary: The daughter of John James of Monferrato and Joan of Savoy, he married Ludovico I of Saluzzo. His son Ludovico II thus gathered ancestry from the Saluzzo, the Italian Paleologists and the Savoy.
ISABELMONSAL.biography: The daughter of Juan James of Monferrato and Joan of Savoy, she married Ludovico I of Saluzzo. Her son Ludovico II thus gathered ancestry from the Saluzzo, the Italian Paleologists and the Savoy. This family combination allows us to understand the Marquis’ ties with his neighbors, even if the kinship did not suppress rivalries over territories and inheritances.

LEOPOLDLORENA.name: Leopold of Lorraine
LEOPOLDLORENA.summary: The Treaty of Ryswick restored the Duchy of Lorraine to him in 1697, and he ruled it until 1729. He was the father of Francis Stephen, husband of Maria Theresa and Holy Roman emperor.

governmentNotes.Dignidad ducal heredada en 1690, sin rec: Ducal dignity inherited in 1690, without effective recovery from the ducats to Ryswick in 1697.
governmentNotes.Restitución efectiva de 1697; la ocupaci: Effective restitution of 1697; the occupation of Nancy in 1702 does not extinguish the entire government from Lunéville.

CATVALCOUR.name: Catherine II of Valois-Courtenay
CATVALCOUR.summary: The daughter of Charles of Valois and Catherine of Courtenay, inherited the title of Latin Empress of Constantinople, already without territory. Married to Philip of Tarento, she resided in the Angevin court of Naples.

CHARLOTTEBOURBONCYP.name: Charlotte of Bourbon, Queen of Cyprus
aliases: Charlotte de Bourbon, Queen of Cyprus
CHARLOTTEBOURBONCYP.summary: The daughter of John of Bourbon-La Marche and Catherine of Vendôme, she married Janus. She was the mother of John II and Anne of Cyprus. This union directly connects the Lusignans with the Bourbons and, by Anne, with the Savoy dynasty.

ANDRES1ANJOU.name: Andrew, Duke of Calabria
ANDRES1ANJOU.summary: A consort of House Anjou-Hungary whose life was connected with Naples.

MARGPROV.name: Margaret of Provence
MARGPROV.summary: A consort of House Barcelona whose life was connected with France.

WILLIAM4HESSE.name: William IV of Hesse-Kassel
WILLIAM4HESSE.summary: First Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel after the partition of the heritage of Philip I. His branch became one of the most durable and active princely houses in the center of Germany.

ROGERBERNARD3FOIX.name: Roger Bernard III of Foix
ROGERBERNARD3FOIX.summary: His marriage to Margaret of Béarn linked the county of Foix with the rights over the Viscounty of the Bearnes. The accumulation of both estates gave his descendants a weighty position on both sides of the Pyrenees.
ROGERBERNARD3FOIX.biography: His marriage to Margaret of Béarn linked the county of Foix with the rights over the Viscounty of Bearnes. The accumulation of both estates gave his descendants a position of weight on both sides of the Pyrenees. Count of Foix and Viscount of Bearne are kept separate in the Atlas.

governmentNotes.Derechos transmitidos por Margarita de B: Rights transmitted by Margaret of Béarn.

RUSUDANGEO.name: Rusudan of Georgia
RUSUDANGEO.summary: The Khwarazmian invasion and subsequent Mongol pressure broke the position achieved by her mother Tamar. Rusudan’s reign marks Georgia’s transition from expansion to tribute and outside intervention in the succession.

JOHN2TREB.name: John II of Trebizond
JOHN2TREB.summary: He negotiated with Michael VIII the scope of the imperial title of Trebizond and married his daughter Eudoxia. His reign was interrupted by the seizure of power of Theodora and shows the autonomy of this court against Constantinople.

LOUISEJULIANANASSAU.name: Louise Juliana of Orange-Nassau
LOUISEJULIANANASSAU.summary: A consort of House Nassau whose life was connected with Netherlands, Palatinate.

AUGUSTWILPRU.name: Prince Augustus William of Prussia
AUGUSTWILPRU.summary: A prince of House Hohenzollern whose life was connected with Prussia.

MARIAGUELDJUL.name: Maria of Guelders, Duchess of Jülich
MARIAGUELDJUL.summary: A daughter of Reinald II, she married William of Jülich and transmitted rights in Guelders to her children. Her position explains the accession of the House of Jülich after her brothers’ deaths; Arnold of Egmond’s hereditary claim also descended from her.

JOHN5NASSAU.name: John V of Nassau-Siegen
JOHN5NASSAU.summary: Earl of Nassau, 1475–1516. Earl of the Nassau dynasty.

SIGFRANZTIROL.name: Sigismund Francis of Austria-Tyrol
SIGFRANZTIROL.summary: Sigismund Francis succeeded his brother Ferdinand Charles in 1662. His death without a male heir in 1665 ended the Tyrolean branch, and the county passed to Leopold I.

governmentNotes.Último gobernante varón de la rama tirol: Last male ruler of the Tyrolean branch; Tyrol passed to Leopold I after his death.

ULRICALEONORADIN.name: Ulrika Eleonora of Denmark
ULRICALEONORADIN.summary: A consort of House Oldenburg whose life was connected with Denmark, Sweden.

ERNSTSAX.name: Ernest of Saxony
ERNSTSAX.summary: Elector of Saxony from 1464. In the Leipzig partition of 1485, he and his brother Albert founded the Ernestine and Albertine lines of the House of Wettin; the Ernestine branch retained the electoral dignity until 1547.

ERICMAGNUSSONSUE.name: Erik Magnusson of Sweden
ERICMAGNUSSONSUE.summary: The son of Magnus III and brother of King Birger. His rivalry with Birger was part of a family crisis that ended with his captivity and death. His marriage to Ingeborg of Norway was decisive: his son Magnus gathered in 1319 the Norwegian heritage and the Swedish election.

GERALD11KILDARE.name: Gerald FitzGerald, XI Earl of Kildare
GERALD11KILDARE.summary: He survived the fall of his family by protecting relatives and allies in Ireland and the continent. He regained the title under Mary Tudor, although the Fitzgeralds no longer enjoyed former political autonomy.

SMBATARM.name: Smbat of Cilician Armenia
SMBATARM.summary: He took advantage of the absence of his brothers to take the crown. Inner struggles weakened the position of the kingdom vis-à-vis its neighbours and ended with its deposition. His brief government is part of the succession crisis of the sons of Leo II.

GIORGIPRINCEGEO.name: George, Prince of Georgia
GIORGIPRINCEGEO.summary: Son of Constantine I and father of Bagrat VI. His position in genealogy allows us to understand that the branch that ended up ruling Imereti came from the Georgian royal family itself, even though it faced other descendants of that house.

MARYSTUARTORANGE.name: Mary, Princess Royal and Princess of Orange
MARYSTUARTORANGE.summary: A princess of orange of House Estuardo whose life was connected with England, Netherlands.

JUANAARAG.name: Joanna of Aragon
JUANAARAG.summary: A consort of House Trastámara whose life was connected with Naples.

LEO3CILICIA.name: Leo III of Cilician Armenia
LEO3CILICIA.summary: Son of Theodore III, he acceded to the throne under the tutelage of his uncle Hetum II. Both were killed by Mongolian chief Bilarghu. The crisis showed that the alliance with the Mongols did not guarantee the security of the Armenian monarchy.

ARCHILPRINCEIMER.name: Archil, Prince of Imereti
ARCHILPRINCEIMER.summary: Brother of Solomon I and father of Solomon II. His marriage to Helena, daughter of Heracli II, linked the last royal generation of Imereti with the united monarchy of Kartli-Kajetia.

HENRYPIOUSSAX.name: Henry of Saxony
HENRYPIOUSSAX.summary: Henry the Pious succeeded in 1539 his brother George in the Albertine Saxony and introduced the Lutheran Reformation there.

ISABELIBELINCYP.name: Isabella of Ibelin
ISABELIBELINCYP.summary: A consort of House Ibelin whose life was connected with Cyprus, Jerusalem.

FRANCOIS1BRET.name: Francis I of Brittany
FRANCOIS1BRET.summary: Son of John V or VI of Brittany and Joan of France, he inherited the duchy in 1442. His government belongs to the final phase of the Hundred Years' War, when relations between the French and English powers changed. Upon his death, the succession passed to his brother Peter II.

LOUIS1SIC.name: Louis I of Sicily
LOUIS1SIC.summary: He succeeded Peter II during his childhood. Rivalries between Baronial families and Neapolitan pressure weakened the kingdom; his death during an epidemic left the crown to his brother Frederick.

ANNAPRUSSIA.name: Anne of Prussia
ANNAPRUSSIA.summary: A consort of House Hohenzollern whose life was connected with Prussia, Brandenburg.

ULRICHWURTT.name: Ulrich of Württemberg
ULRICHWURTT.summary: Duke of Württemberg whose turbulent government was marked by internal conflicts, expulsion and restoration. Reformation and struggles between Habsburg and imperial princes conditioned his return to power.

MAURICEORANGE.name: Maurice of Orange
MAURICEORANGE.summary: William of Orange’s son Maurice commanded the armies of the United Provinces and served as stadtholder of several provinces. His campaigns consolidated the revolt against the Spanish Monarchy. He inherited the Principality of Orange in 1618 and entered into a political conflict with Johan van Oldenbarnevelt, who was executed in 1619. Maurice died in 1625.

governmentNotes.Cargo provincial delegado por los Estado: Provincial post delegated by the States, with documented personal areas and dates; not hereditary sovereignty over the entire Republic or the Spanish provinces.

TOMAS1SAL.name: Thomas I of Saluzzo
TOMAS1SAL.summary: He inherited from Manfredo III during his minority and made Saluzzo a more stable political center of the marquisate. His mother, Beatrice of Savoy, later married Manfredo of Sicily.
TOMAS1SAL.biography: He inherited from Manfredo III during his minority and made Saluzzo a more stable political center of the marquisate. His mother, Beatrice of Savoy, later married Manfredo of Sicily. For that second marriage, Thomas was half brother of Constance of Sicily: a direct connection between the Alps and later Aragonese royalty.

VLAD4CALUGAR.name: Vlad IV Călugărul
VLAD4CALUGAR.summary: The son of Vlad II Dracul, briefly came to power in 1481 and recovered him the following year. His continuity until 1495 opens a family path different from that of his brother Vlad III. His son Radu the Great extended this Basarab line in the Wallachia government.

CHARLES2ALBRET.name: Charles II of Albret
CHARLES2ALBRET.summary: The son of Count Charles I, he continued the House of Albret after his father’s death at Agincourt. The line through his son John of Tartas led to Alain of Albret and preserves the seigneurial continuity between the fifteenth century and the generation linked to Navarre.

ALBERTINEAGNESORANGE.name: Albertine Agnes of Orange-Nassau
ALBERTINEAGNESORANGE.summary: A consort of House Nassau whose life was connected with Netherlands.

ENRIQUEDARNLEY.name: Henry Stuart, Lord Darnley
ENRIQUEDARNLEY.summary: A consort of House Estuardo whose life was connected with Scotland, England.

ISABBORJA.name: Isabel de Borja
ISABBORJA.summary: A noble of House Borja whose life was connected with Valencia.

JUAN2NEVERS.name: John II of Nevers
JUAN2NEVERS.summary: Count of Nevers, 1464–1491. Count of the Valois-Borgogna dynasty.

CAROLINEMATILDA.name: Caroline Matilda of Great Britain
CAROLINEMATILDA.summary: A consort of House Hanover whose life was connected with England, Denmark.

MARGENGBRAB.name: Margaret of England
MARGENGBRAB.summary: Daughter of Edward I and Leonor of Castile, she married John II of Brabant. She was the mother of John III. Through her, the Brabantine ducal line was connected to England and Castile before her subsequent relationship with the Valois of Burgundy.

BARBJAGSAX.name: Barbara Jagiellon
BARBJAGSAX.summary: A consort of House Jagelón whose life was connected with Poland, Lithuania, Saxony.

CARLOS10GUSTAVO.name: Charles X Gustav of Sweden
CARLOS10GUSTAVO.summary: King of Sweden and commander of a stage of maximum Swedish military expansion. His campaigns in Poland and Denmark temporarily reinforced Sweden’s hegemony in the Baltic.

MARIABORGSAB.name: Maria of Burgundy
MARIABORGSAB.summary: A consort of House Valois-Borgoña whose life was connected with Burgundy, Savoy.

GIORGI3GEO.name: George III of Georgia
GIORGI3GEO.summary: He associated his daughter Tamar with the throne to secure the succession of the Bagrationi. His policy of expansion and his conflicts with the aristocracy set the stage for the Georgian monarchy at the end of the 12th century.

MARGARITAFRANCIASAB.name: Margaret of France
MARGARITAFRANCIASAB.summary: A consort of House Valois-Angulema whose life was connected with France, Savoy.

SANCIABORGIA.name: Sancia of Aragon
SANCIABORGIA.summary: A consort of House Trastámara whose life was connected with Naples, Squillace.

JOHNCICEROBRAND.name: John Cicero of Brandenburg
JOHNCICEROBRAND.summary: Elector of Brandenburg, 1486–1499. Elector of the Hohenzollern dynasty.

GEORGEBRUNSCAL.name: George of Brunswick-Lüneburg
GEORGEBRUNSCAL.summary: Duke of Brunswick, 1635–1641. Duke of the Welf Dynasty.

THOMASPALA.name: Thomas Palaiologos
THOMASPALA.summary: Despot of Morea, 1428–1460. Despot of Morea of the Paleolog dynasty.

ANNEGBORANGE.name: Anne of Great Britain
ANNEGBORANGE.summary: Governor of the Netherlands, 1751–1759 (delegated government). Princess of Orange of the Hannover dynasty.

governmentNotes.Regencia del cargo hereditario de Guille: Regency of the hereditary office of William V during his minority; provincial authority of the States, not sovereign monarchy over the Republic.

CAR1NEVERS.name: Charles I of Nevers
CAR1NEVERS.summary: Count of Nevers, 1415–1464. Count of the Valois-Borgogna dynasty.

CONSTANZAARAGMAL.name: Constance of Aragon
CONSTANZAARAGMAL.summary: A consort of House Barcelona whose life was connected with Majorca, Aragon.

CONSTANCEAUVASA.name: Constance of Austria
CONSTANCEAUVASA.summary: A consort of House Habsburg whose life was connected with Austria, Poland, Lithuania.

BEATSUAB.name: Beatrice of Swabia
BEATSUAB.summary: A consort of House Hohenstaufen whose life was connected with Castile.

FERN2ALBA.name: Fernando Álvarez de Toledo y Pimentel
aliases: Fernando Álvarez de Toledo y Pimentel (Gran Duque de Alba)
FERN2ALBA.summary: Fernando Álvarez de Toledo, 3rd Duke of Alba, was governor general of the Netherlands by Philip II between 1567 and 1573. His repressive policy and the campaigns of revolt marked the government.
FERN2ALBA.biography: His post was delegated and did not make him sovereign of the Netherlands. The provinces retain their identities; the map distinguishes the rebellion of Holland and Zeeland since 1572 and the disputed control of Flanders and Brabant.

governmentNotes.Gobernador general por nombramiento de F: Governor General by appointment of Philip II. The position does not provide uniform control during the revolt; the map distinguishes its disputed areas since 1572.

BEATCAST2.name: Beatrice of Castile
BEATCAST2.summary: A consort of House Ivrea-Borgoña whose life was connected with Portugal.

FERDMARIABAV.name: Ferdinand Maria of Bavaria
FERDMARIABAV.summary: Elector of Bavaria, 1651–1679. Elector of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

FRED1BRAND.name: Frederick I of Brandenburg
FRED1BRAND.summary: Burgrave of Nuremberg, received from Sigismund the government of Brandenburg in 1415 and the investiture as Elector in 1417. He was the first Hohenzollern to head the electorate.

ANNECATHBRANDDEN.name: Anne Catherine of Brandenburg
ANNECATHBRANDDEN.summary: A consort of House Hohenzollern whose life was connected with Brandenburg, Denmark.

ISABELBAVCAR.name: Elizabeth of Bavaria
ISABELBAVCAR.summary: A consort of House Wittelsbach whose life was connected with Bavaria, Tyrol, Carinthia.

JUANGEORGEBRAND.name: John George of Brandenburg
JUANGEORGEBRAND.summary: Elector of Brandenburg, 1571–1598. Elector of the Hohenzollern dynasty.

EUDOKIAPALEOTREB.name: Eudokia Palaiologina of Trebizond
EUDOKIAPALEOTREB.summary: The daughter of Michael VIII and sister of Andronico II, his marriage to John II brought together the courts of Constantinople and Trebizond. He supported the Georgian marriage of his son Alejo II, linking the Palaiologists to the networks of the Caucasus.

RAMONROGERFOIX.name: Raymond Roger of Foix
RAMONROGERFOIX.summary: Count of Foix since 1188 and protector of the Cathars during the Albigense crusade. In 1213 he paid homage to Peter II of Aragon for his castles and fought next to him in Muret. He died in 1223.

governmentNotes.En 1213 rindió homenaje a Pedro II de Ar: In 1213 he paid homage to Pedro II of Aragon for his castles and fought alongside him in Muret.

MARIAMOL.name: María de Molina
MARIAMOL.summary: A consort of House Ivrea-Borgoña whose life was connected with Castile.

BOGISLAW13POM.name: Bogislaw XIII of Pomerania
BOGISLAW13POM.summary: Duke of Pomerania, 1603-106. Duke of the Griph dynasty.

ANNADENMARKSAX.name: Anne of Denmark
ANNADENMARKSAX.summary: A consort of House Oldenburg whose life was connected with Denmark, Saxony.

ENRIQ3BR.name: Henry III of Brabant
ENRIQ3BR.summary: Duke of Brabant, 1248–1261. Duke of the Brabant dynasty.

BAGRAT1MUKHRANI.name: Bagrat I of Mukhrani
BAGRAT1MUKHRANI.summary: Son of Constantine II, he founded the princely branch of Mukhrani. His descendants reached the crown of Kartli with Vajtang V, so this line does not appear as a family isolated from the royal trunk.

ODOARDO1FARN.name: Odoardo I Farnese
ODOARDO1FARN.summary: Duke of Parma, 1622–1646. Duke of the Farnesian dynasty.

JAIME1BRAG.name: Jaime I of Braganza
JAIME1BRAG.summary: A duke of House Braganza whose life was connected with Portugal.

SIMONIMER.name: Simon of Imereti
SIMONIMER.summary: Son of Alexander IV, briefly occupied a crown disputed by great lords and candidates Bagrationi. His murder opened another phase of intervention by the Gurieli and Abashidze in the government of Imereti.

ERIKJOHVASA.name: Erik Johansson Vasa
ERIKJOHVASA.summary: Noble Swede and the father of Gustavo Vasa. He was executed in the bloodbath in Stockholm in 1520. His death belongs to the context of his son's rebellion against Cristian II; Gustavo's access to the throne was the result of that struggle and an election, not the inheritance of a paternal crown.

BOUCHARDAVES.name: Bouchard of Avesnes
BOUCHARDAVES.summary: His marriage to Margaret II of Flanders founded the Avesnes line. The dispute over the marriage’s validity affected his children’s rights and became part of the succession conflict between the Avesnes and Dampierre branches.

FABRCOLONNA.name: Fabrizio Colonna
FABRCOLONNA.summary: A condottiere of House Colonna whose life was connected with Naples, Pontifical States.

CLAUDEFRALOR.name: Claude of Valois
CLAUDEFRALOR.summary: A consort of House Valois-Angulema whose life was connected with France, Lorraine.

ISABLUX.name: Elizabeth of Luxembourg
ISABLUX.summary: A consort of House Luxembourg whose life was connected with Hungary, Bohemia.

SOLOMON1IMER.name: Solomon I of Imereti
SOLOMON1IMER.summary: He tried to limit the power of the great lords and combat the slave trade. Khresili’s victory reinforced his position against the Ottomans, although he suffered a temporary deposition. His policy sought greater autonomy for the Western monarchy.

MARIACLEVES.name: Maria of Cleves
MARIACLEVES.summary: A consort of House La Marck whose life was connected with France, Cléneris.

MARGABRAB1323.name: Margaret of Brabant
MARGABRAB1323.summary: A consort of House Brabant whose life was connected with Flanders, Brabant.

BLANBRET.name: Blanche of Brittany
BLANBRET.summary: The daughter of John II of Brittany and Beatrice of England, she married Philip of Artois. Her offspring linked with the Évreux through Margaret of Artois. The Brittany-Artois-Évreux chain constitutes an important family connection between the Atlantic Duchy and the Navarrese monarchy.

JUAN8VENDOME.name: John VIII of Vendôme
JUAN8VENDOME.summary: Count of Vendôme, 1446–1477. Count of the Bourbon dynasty.

JEANDUNOIS.name: Jean de Dunois
JEANDUNOIS.summary: A count of House Valois-Orleans whose life was connected with France, Orleans.

CARLOS3LOR.name: Charles III of Lorraine
CARLOS3LOR.summary: Duke of Lorraine, 1545–1608. Duke of the Lorraine dynasty.

HELVISBRUNSCYP.name: Helvis of Brunswick-Grubenhagen
HELVISBRUNSCYP.summary: He shared with James I the Genoese captivity, during which Janus was born. As queen of Cyprus he linked the Lusignans with the house of Welf. The family experience of captivity marked the next generation of the monarchy.

ROSTOMIMER.name: Rostom of Imereti
ROSTOMIMER.summary: He depended on Mingrelia's backing to attain and regain the throne. His reign included a break during the intervention of Simon of Kartli and his Western rivals, so two mandates are recorded.

LUIS7FRA.name: Louis VII of France
LUIS7FRA.summary: The son and successor of Louis VI, he was the father of Philip II and brother of Robert I of Dreux. His position links the main line of the Capetian kings with the comital branch.
LUIS7FRA.biography: The son and successor of Louis VI, he was the father of Philip II and brother of Robert I of Dreux. His position links the main line of the Capetian kings with the comital branch. The transmission of the crown to Philip II continued on a different path than that which would lead the descendants of Robert to the Duchy of Brittany.

JUANA2BORG.name: Joan II of Burgundy
JUANA2BORG.summary: She was Queen Consort of France and holder of the county of Burgundy by inheritance. Her career forces her to distinguish her marital dignity from her own territorial rights.

MAX3JOSEBAV.name: Maximilian III Joseph of Bavaria
MAX3JOSEBAV.summary: Elector of Bavaria, 1745–1777. Elector of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

governmentNotes.Sucede a su padre, el emperador Carlos V: It happens to his father, Emperor Charles VII, in 1745. Last elector of the Bavarian line of the Wittelsbach; upon his death Bavaria passes to Charles Theodore.

PEDRO1BOR.name: Peter I of Bourbon
PEDRO1BOR.summary: He participated in the Hundred Years' War in the service of the French monarchy. He died in Poitiers, where John II of France fell prisoner.

AGNESPALBAV.name: Agnes of the Palatinate
AGNESPALBAV.summary: A consort of House Welf whose life was connected with Bavaria, Palatinate.

JOHANNJULARKEL.name: Joanna of Jülich
JOHANNJULARKEL.summary: Sister of William I and Reinald IV of Guelders, she was the mother of Mary of Arkel. Her offspring explain the claim of Arnold of Egmond in 1423. The succession was not a direct relationship of father and son between Reinaldo and Arnoldo.

VALDEMAR2DEN.name: Valdemar II of Denmark
VALDEMAR2DEN.summary: King of Denmark since 1202. He conquered Estonia in 1219; after his defeat in Bornhöved (1227) he lost almost all his possessions in northern Germany. He promulgated the law of Jutland.

governmentNotes.Reinado documentado en la cronología ofi: Reign documented in the Danish official chronology.

MATTEOROSSOORS_GRANDE.name: Matteo Rosso Orsini
MATTEOROSSOORS_GRANDE.summary: A senador of House Orsini whose life was connected with Rome.

ENRIQENRIQUEZ.name: Henry Enríquez de Quiñones
ENRIQENRIQUEZ.summary: A noble of House Enriquez whose life was connected with Castile.

CHRISTIANAUGUSTEUTIN.name: Christian August of Holstein-Gottorp-Eutin
CHRISTIANAUGUSTEUTIN.summary: A príncipe-obispo of House Holstein-Gottorp whose life was connected with Holstein.

CONSTPORT.name: Constance of Portugal
CONSTPORT.summary: A consort of House Burgundy-Portugal whose life was connected with Castile.

ANNAPETROVNA.name: Anna Petrovna of Russia
ANNAPETROVNA.summary: A duchess of House Romanov whose life was connected with Russia, Holstein.

JAIME1MARCH.name: James I of Bourbon-La Marche
JAIME1MARCH.summary: Count of La Marche, 1342–1362. Count of the Bourbon dynasty.

STEFANNEMANJASER.name: Stefan Nemanja
STEFANNEMANJASER.summary: Great župan of Serbia, 1166–1196. Great župan of the Nemanjić dynasty.

BLANCANAVCHAMP.name: Blanche of Navarre
BLANCANAVCHAMP.summary: Daughter of Sancho VI and sister of Sancho VII, she married Teobaldo III of Champagne. After widowing she held the position of her son Teobaldo during her minority. For her, that son gathered a Navarrese hereditary right that became effective when his uncle Sancho VII died.

GIORGI9KARTLI.name: George IX of Kartli
GIORGI9KARTLI.summary: Brother of David X, he assumed the crown after his abdication and gave it to his nephew Luarsab. His brief government links two generations of the Bagrationi in a period of increasing Persian intervention.

AGNESHOHENPAL.name: Agnes of Hohenstaufen
AGNESHOHENPAL.summary: A consort of House Hohenstaufen whose life was connected with Palatinate.

BEATSIL.name: Beatrice of Silesia
BEATSIL.summary: A consort of House Piast whose life was connected with Germany, Bavaria.

ALFONSOMONTECCHIOESTE.name: Alfonso d’Este
ALFONSOMONTECCHIOESTE.summary: A marquess of House East whose life was connected with Modena.

SOPHIAPALMOSC.name: Sophia Palaiologina
SOPHIAPALMOSC.summary: A consort of House Paleologist whose life was connected with Byzantium, Russia.

MARIACRISTINASAJCAR.name: Maria Christina Albertina of Saxony
MARIACRISTINASAJCAR.summary: A princess of carignano of House Wettin whose life was connected with Saxony, Savoy.

CARLOS3PHILIPPAL.name: Charles III Philip of the Palatinate-Neuburg
CARLOS3PHILIPPAL.summary: Duke of Palatinate-Neoburg, 1716–1742. Elector of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

governmentNotes.Sucede a su hermano Juan Guillermo en 17: It happens to his brother John William in 1716 in the Palatinate and in the Duchys of Newenburg, Jülich and Berg.

MICVAL.name: Michelle of Valois
MICVAL.summary: A consort of House Valois whose life was connected with Burgundy, France.

JOHNBEAUFORT1.name: John Beaufort
JOHNBEAUFORT1.summary: The son of John of Ghent and Catherine of Roet, he was legitimized along with his brothers in 1397 and received the county of Somerset. He was the father of Duke John Beaufort and grandfather of Margaret Beaufort, mother of Henry VII.

CUNH.name: Kunigunda of Halych
CUNH.summary: A consort of House Rurikida whose life was connected with Bohemia.

ENGELBERT1NASSAU.name: Engelbert I of Nassau
ENGELBERT1NASSAU.summary: Earl of Nassau, 1416–1442. Earl of the Nassau dynasty.

FED1BAV.name: Frederick of Bavaria-Landshut
FED1BAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria, 1375–1393 (rama), Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

FRED1MEISSEN.name: Frederick I of Meißen
FRED1MEISSEN.summary: Margrave of Meißen, 1307–1323. Margrave of the Wettin dynasty.

IVAN5RUS.name: Ivan V of Russia
IVAN5RUS.summary: Tsar of Russia, 1682–1696 (corregent). Tsar of the Romanov dynasty.

IPPOLITOMEDICI.name: Ippolito de’ Medici
IPPOLITOMEDICI.summary: A cardinal of House Medici whose life was connected with Florence, Pontifical States.

MARIAARAG.name: Maria of Aragon
MARIAARAG.summary: A consort of House Trastámara whose life was connected with Castile.

JOHN4NASSAU.name: John IV of Nassau-Breda
JOHN4NASSAU.summary: Earl of Nassau, 1442–1475. Earl of the Nassau dynasty.

FRED5BADEN.name: Frederick V of Baden-Durlach
FRED5BADEN.summary: Margrave of Baden, 1622–1659. Margrave of the Zähringen-Baden dynasty.

SOPHIEMAGDKULM.name: Sophie Magdalene of Brandenburg-Kulmbach
SOPHIEMAGDKULM.summary: A consort of House Hohenzollern whose life was connected with Brandenburg, Denmark.

HAAKON4NOR.name: Haakon IV of Norway
HAAKON4NOR.summary: His reign closed the long period of Norwegian civil wars and reinforced the monarchy. The expansion to Iceland and Greenland expanded its Atlantic horizon. His son Magnus VI continued the dynasty; by that line descended Haakon V, Ingeborg of Norway and the kings who gathered Norway and Sweden.

JUANPORTINF.name: John Manuel of Portugal
JUANPORTINF.summary: A prince of House Notice whose life was connected with Portugal.

LUISTARANTONAP.name: Louis of Taranto
LUISTARANTONAP.summary: Second husband of Joan I of Naples, he tried to impose his authority on the government of the kingdom. His shared reign coincided with the Hungarian invasions and the search for legitimacy following the murder of Andrew of Anjou.

WILHELM2JUL.name: William II of Jülich
WILHELM2JUL.summary: His marriage to Mary of Guelders gave his children a position in the succession of the neighbouring duchy. The connection did not come from an automatic conquest or from the name of Jülich, but from the rights of Mary. William and Reinaldo, the sons of both, ruled Guelders successively.

MURAD2OSM.name: Murad II
MURAD2OSM.summary: Ottoman Sultan who consolidated the rule of his dynasty in the Balkans before the conquest of Constantinople. His victories over crusaders and regional rivals set the stage for the reign of his son Mehmed II.

CARLOTAJOAQ.name: Carlota Joaquina of Spain
CARLOTAJOAQ.summary: A consort of House Bourbon whose life was connected with Portugal, Spain.

WALTER11ORMOND.name: Walter Butler, XI Earl of Ormond
WALTER11ORMOND.summary: He succeeded his uncle Thomas in the title, but he litigated for properties attributed largely to another family branch. His grandson James' marriage to Elizabeth Preston helped to re-compose that divided heritage.

CONSTARAG.name: Constance of Aragon
CONSTARAG.summary: A noble of House Barcelona whose life was connected with Castile.

MARGBAUX.name: Margaret of Taranto
MARGBAUX.summary: A princess of House Anjou-Tarento whose life was connected with Naples, Tarento.

MARIELOUISEHESSE.name: Marie Louise of Hesse-Kassel
MARIELOUISEHESSE.summary: A consort of House Hesse whose life was connected with Hesse, Netherlands.

KATHBRANDK.name: Catherine of Brandenburg-Küstrin
KATHBRANDK.summary: A consort of House Hohenzollern whose life was connected with Brandenburg.

CHARLOTTEBOURBONORANGE.name: Charlotte of Bourbon-Montpensier
CHARLOTTEBOURBONORANGE.summary: A consort of House Bourbon whose life was connected with France, Netherlands.

ANNAMARIALUISAMEDICI.name: Anna Maria Luisa de’ Medici
ANNAMARIALUISAMEDICI.summary: An electress consort of House Medici whose life was connected with Tuscany, Palatinate.

ELIZABETHPETROVNA.name: Elizabeth of Russia
ELIZABETHPETROVNA.summary: Empress of Russia and daughter of Peter the Great. Her reign consolidated the European position of the empire and was marked by Russian participation in the Seven Years War.

BEATBOR.name: Beatrice of Bourbon
BEATBOR.summary: A consort of House Bourbon whose life was connected with Bohemia.

FRED2WURTT.name: Frederick II of Württemberg
FRED2WURTT.summary: Duke of Württemberg, 1797–1803. Duke of the Württemberg dynasty.

governmentNotes.Sucede a su padre el 23 de diciembre de: He succeeded his father on December 23, 1797. Elector since 1803 and king of Württemberg, as Frederick I, since January 1, 1806.

ALB2MEISSEN.name: Albert II of Meissen
ALB2MEISSEN.summary: Landgrave of Thuringia, 1265–1307. Landgrave of the Wettin dynasty.

MAX4JOSEBAV.name: Maximilian IV Joseph of Bavaria
MAX4JOSEBAV.summary: Elector of Bavaria, 1799–1806. Elector of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

governmentNotes.Asume Pfalzbayern a la muerte de Carlos: Assume Pfalzbayern to the death of Charles Theodore (16 February 1799). King of Bavaria, as Maximilian I Joseph, since 1 January 1806.
governmentNotes.En 1801 cede a Francia los territorios p: In 1801, the Palatine territories of the left bank of the Rhine, which had been occupied for years, were ceded to France; it remained on the right bank until the rearrangement of 1803.
governmentNotes.Renuncia a Berg en el reparto que sigue: He renounced Berg in the division following the peace of Presburg (26 December 1805).

JUANAKENT.name: Joan of Kent
JUANAKENT.summary: A noble of House Plantagenet whose life was connected with England.

CLAUDIAFELICITAS.name: Claudia Felicitas of Austria
CLAUDIAFELICITAS.summary: A consort of House Habsburg whose life was connected with Holy Empire, Austria.

PETER2RUS.name: Peter II of Russia
PETER2RUS.summary: Grandson of Peter the Great, emperor of Russia since 1727. He moved the court back to Moscow and died of smallpox at the age of fourteen, extinguishing the male line of the Romanovs.

STEFANVLAD1SER.name: Stefan Vladislav I of Serbia
STEFANVLAD1SER.summary: King of Serbia between 1234 and 1243 after displacing his brother Radoslav. He was in turn replaced by his younger brother, Stephen Uroš I.

RAMON6TOLOSA.name: Raymond VI of Toulouse
RAMON6TOLOSA.summary: Count of Tolosa since 1194 and protector of the Cathars, was excommunicated after the assassination of the legacy Pierre de Castelnau (1208), who triggered the Albigense crusade. In 1213 he swore fidelity to Peter II of Aragon, whose death in Muret left the Languedoc to Simon de Montfort. Dismissed in 1215, he recovered Toulouse in 1217 and died in 1222. He married in 1196 to Joan of England and, widowed, to Leonor of Aragon, sister of Peter II.

governmentNotes.En 1213 juró fidelidad a Pedro II de Ara: In 1213 he swore allegiance to Peter II of Aragon. The Lateran Council dispossessed him in 1215 in favor of Simon of Montfort; he recovered Toulouse in 1217.

AUGUSTASAXGOTHA.name: Augusta of Saxe-Gotha
AUGUSTASAXGOTHA.summary: A consort of House Wettin whose life was connected with Saxony, England.

DAVIDHUNTINGDON.name: David of Scotland, Count of Huntingdon
DAVIDHUNTINGDON.summary: Count of Huntingdon, 1185–1219. Prince of the Dunkeld dynasty.

REIN2GUELD.name: Reinald II of Guelders
REIN2GUELD.summary: He ruled Guelders first as count and then as duke after the territory was raised to a duchy in 1339. The succession set his sons Reinald and Edward against one another and later involved the descendants of his daughters. Distinguishing the county from the duchy preserves that change in rank.

ANNEELEANORHESSE.name: Anne Eleanor of Hesse-Darmstadt
ANNEELEANORHESSE.summary: A consort of House Hesse whose life was connected with Hesse, Brunswick.

CATALANC.name: Catherine of Lancaster
CATALANC.summary: A consort of House Plantagenet-Lancaster whose life was connected with Castile.

LUDWIG7HESSEDARM.name: Louis VII of Hesse-Darmstadt
LUDWIG7HESSEDARM.summary: Landgrave of Hesse-Darmstadt, 1678–1678. Landgrave of the Hesse dynasty.

governmentNotes.Sucede a su padre en abril de 1678 y mue: He succeeded his father in April 1678 and died in August, after about four months of government.

CATHCOUR.name: Catherine of Courtenay
CATHCOUR.summary: A consort of House Courtenay whose life was connected with Latin Empire.

THOMASTHURLES.name: Thomas Butler, Viscount Thurles
THOMASTHURLES.summary: Son of Walter Butler and father of the future Duke of Ormond. He died in a shipwreck before inheriting the county, so the succession passed directly from his father to his son James.

ENRIQUEGROSMONT.name: Henry of Grosmont
ENRIQUEGROSMONT.summary: A duke of House Plantagenet-Lancaster whose life was connected with England, Aquitaine.

OTON4BORG.name: Otto IV of Burgundy
OTON4BORG.summary: He ruled the county of Burgundy, different from the duchy of the same name. His marriage agreements with the French monarchy had lasting consequences for the succession of the Franche-Comté.

COSTEAMUSAT.name: Costea Mușat
COSTEAMUSAT.summary: A noble of House Bogdan-Mușat whose life was connected with Moldova.

ISABELNUR.name: Elisabeth of Nuremberg
ISABELNUR.summary: A consort of House Hohenzollern whose life was connected with Germany, Palatinate.

RENATALORENA.name: Renata of Lorraine
RENATALORENA.summary: A consort of House Lorraine whose life was connected with Bavaria, Lorraine.

ENRIQ1BR.name: Henry I of Brabant
ENRIQ1BR.summary: Duke of Brabant, 1183–1235. Duke of the Brabant dynasty.

LEONSANCH.name: Leonor Sánchez of Castile
LEONSANCH.summary: A noble of House Ivrea-Borgoña whose life was connected with Castile.

CRISTINAHESSECAR.name: Christine Henriette of Hesse-Rotenburg
CRISTINAHESSECAR.summary: A princess of carignano of House Hesse whose life was connected with Hesse, Savoy.

CHRISTOPHERBATH.name: Christopher Báthory
CHRISTOPHERBATH.summary: Brother of Stephen Bathory, he led Transylvania as a voivode while he reigned in Poland and retained princely dignity. His son Sigismund inherited a position marked by that overlapping of functions.

LUISAMARIAGONZAGA.name: Louise Marie Gonzaga
LUISAMARIAGONZAGA.summary: Princess of the house of Gonzaga-Nevers, was queen of Poland as the successor wife of Ladislaus IV and his brother John II Casimiro, over whose politics he had great influence.

MEINHARDBAV.name: Meinhard of Bavaria
MEINHARDBAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria, 1361–1363 (rama), Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

MARIABORBON.name: Mary of Bourbon
MARIABORBON.summary: A consort of House Bourbon whose life was connected with Naples.

FELCOUR.name: Philip of Courtenay
FELCOUR.summary: Son of Baldwin II, last Latin emperor of Constantinople. After the Byzantine reconquest of 1261 he inherited only the title and married Beatrice, daughter of Charles of Anjou.

MATHILDEHESSECLEVES.name: Mathilde of Hesse
MATHILDEHESSECLEVES.summary: Mathilde of Hesse married John II of Cléveris; his son John III linked Cléveris-Mark with the inheritance of Jülich-Berg-Ravensberg.

ROBERTO2TAR.name: Robert of Taranto
ROBERTO2TAR.summary: Prince of Tarento, 1332–1364. Prince of the Anjou-Tarento dynasty.

AEDHFELIMCONN.name: Áed Ua Conchobair
AEDHFELIMCONN.summary: He succeeded his father Fedlimid and fought the Burgh expansion in Connacht. His victory in Áth an Chip in 1270 temporarily stopped his advance. Disputes between branches of his own family continued after his death.

ALFPORT.name: Afonso of Portugal
ALFPORT.summary: An infante of House Burgundy-Portugal whose life was connected with Portugal.

MEHMED3OSM.name: Mehmed III
MEHMED3OSM.summary: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire, 1595–1603. Sultan of the Osmanli dynasty.

CATHAB.name: Catherine of Habsburg
CATHAB.summary: A consort of House Habsburg whose life was connected with Bavaria.

SIBILA1PALLARS.name: Sibylla I of Pallars
SIBILA1PALLARS.summary: Daughter of Arnaldo Roger I, was Countess of Pallars from 1295 to 1330 against the claims of the Coserans, with the support of Jaime II. In 1297 he married Hugo de Mataplana, who ruled with her.

MAXPHILBAV.name: Maximilian Philip Hieronymus of Bavaria-Leuchtenberg
MAXPHILBAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria, 1666–1705 (rama), Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

ABELDEN.name: Abel of Denmark
ABELDEN.summary: King of Denmark since 1250, suspected of having ordered the death of his brother Erik IV. He died in 1252 in a campaign against the Frisians.

governmentNotes.Reinado documentado en la cronología ofi: Reign documented in the Danish official chronology.

RAMON7TOLOSA.name: Raymond VII of Toulouse
RAMON7TOLOSA.summary: The son of Raymond VI and Joan of England, he married Sancha of Aragon in 1211. He helped his father recover Toulouse from the Montforts and succeeded him in 1222; under the Treaty of Paris of 1229 he accepted terms that shaped the county’s later succession.

governmentNotes.Por el tratado de París (1229) el condad: By the Treaty of Paris (1229) the county was destined to her daughter Joan and her son-in-law Alphonse of Poitiers.

EBERHARD3WURTT.name: Eberhard III of Württemberg
EBERHARD3WURTT.summary: Count of Württemberg, 1392–1417. Count of the Württemberg dynasty.

KONSTCZART.name: Konstancja Czartoryska
KONSTCZART.summary: A noble of House Czartoryski whose life was connected with Poland, Lithuania.

MARJORIEBRUCE.name: Marjorie Bruce
MARJORIEBRUCE.summary: A princess of House Bruce. whose life was connected with Scotland.

LUDMILABOHBAV.name: Ludmila of Bohemia
LUDMILABOHBAV.summary: A consort of House Přemysl whose life was connected with Bohemia, Bavaria.

SOPHIELEGNICA.name: Sophia of Legnica
SOPHIELEGNICA.summary: A consort of House Piast whose life was connected with Silesia, Brandenburg.

JUANVELASCO.name: Juan Fernández de Velasco y Tovar
JUANVELASCO.summary: A duke of House Velasco whose life was connected with Castile.

ALFVAL.name: Alfonso of Valencia
ALFVAL.summary: A lord of House Ivrea-Borgoña whose life was connected with Castile.

INGEGERDBIRGERSUE.name: Ingegerd Birgersdotter
INGEGERDBIRGERSUE.summary: A consort of House Bjälbo whose life was connected with Sweden.

PREM2.name: Przemysł II of Poland
PREM2.summary: His coronation represented an attempt to restore the unity of the Polish kingdom after the fragmentation into ducats. He was killed shortly afterwards, leaving the successor dispute open.

ROBERTBRUS6.name: Robert de Brus
ROBERTBRUS6.summary: Lord of Annandale, 1295–1304. Lord of Annandale of the Bruce Dynasty.

CIMBURGISMAZ.name: Cymburgis of Masovia
CIMBURGISMAZ.summary: A consort of House Piast whose life was connected with Austria, Mazovia.

JAIMEBAUX.name: James of Baux
JAIMEBAUX.summary: A prince of House Baux whose life was connected with Naples.

LUISAISABELORL.name: Louise Élisabeth of Orléans
LUISAISABELORL.summary: A consort of House Bourbon-Orleans whose life was connected with Spain, France.

ROMANYURIEVICH.name: Roman Zakharyin-Yuriev
ROMANYURIEVICH.summary: A boyar of House Romanov whose life was connected with Russia.

PAPA_BENEDICTO13.name: Benedict XIII
PAPA_BENEDICTO13.summary: Pietro Francesco Orsini, Dominican and Archbishop of Benevento, was pope between 1724 and 1730. He left the government in the hands of his secretary, Cardinal Niccolò Coscia.

TOMMOCENIGODOGE.name: Tommaso Mocenigo
TOMMOCENIGODOGE.summary: Dogo elected from the Republic of Venice, 1414–1423. The magistracy was not hereditary; the territories on the map belonged to the Republic.

governmentNotes.Magistratura electiva de la República de: Elective judiciary of the Republic of Venice; the domains drawn belong to the Republic, not to the personal heritage of the dogo.

ROB3ART.name: Robert III of Artois
ROB3ART.summary: A count of House Artois whose life was connected with France.
